reuse.why: All month-wide actions keep going through the existing shouldFillCategory/getFillCategories selection and the new action reuses averageToBudgetAmount, but the #fixed test hand-rolls a tag regex instead of using the shared extractTagsFromText in shared/tags.ts.

duplication.why: The `includeHiddenCategories ? 'include' : <default>` mapping is repeated in five actions and the group-notes join is added to both getBudgetData and getFillCategories; setLastMonthSpending repeats the per-category loop shape of the n-month average actions.

placement.why: The template and #fixed exclusions sit inside the single fill-selection predicate in budget/actions.ts, and the new handler is registered next to its siblings in budget/app.ts.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the month-wide action selection, the new action, its registration, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: The exclusion rules are centralised, but how the opt-in flag maps to each action's hidden rule is decided at every call site, and a private tag parser can drift from the app's own tag syntax.

bypasses_abstraction.where: isFixedGroup in server/budget/actions.ts parses `#fixed` with its own regex instead of shared/tags.ts extractTagsFromText.

disguised_duplication.where: isFixedGroup's /(^|\s)#fixed(?![\w-])/ re-expresses the tag extraction already defined in extractTagsFromText with a different shape and slightly different boundary rules.

abstraction_drift.where: shouldFillCategory gains template and #fixed branches (rule additions, kept inside the shared helper); the includeHiddenCategories flag is not given to the helper, so copyPreviousMonth, setZero, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg, set12MonthAvg and setLastMonthSpending each compute their own hiddenRule ternary.
